% Shared normative core: requirements, predictions, and authored options
\section{Normative requirements}
\label{sec:requirements}

\begin{longtable}{p{0.25\linewidth}p{0.65\linewidth}}
\toprule
Requirement & Normative statement \\
\midrule
\endhead
\Req{001} & The method identity shall be \ContractID{}, titled ``Optimal
matched-template map filtering,'' subject to the qualified optimality rule in
Section~\ref{sec:optimality}. \\
\Req{002} & The sole estimand shall be local amplitude of one exact supplied
template; the public signal shall be a filtered amplitude map. \\
\Req{003} & Each application shall bind exactly one immutable normalized
ordinary-MAP observation parent or exactly one immutable normalized
ordinary-MAP coadd parent. JINC and other derived parents are excluded. \\
\Req{004} & Observation and coadd applications shall remain distinct; no
commutation, equivalence, state sharing, or FLT-owned coaddition may be
asserted. \\
\Req{005} & Each application shall bind one immutable materialized template-
response product expressing expected parent-map response per unit amplitude,
with exact scale, phase, anchor, sampling, support, and lineage. \\
\Req{006} & The template shall not be learned or updated from a target,
source, candidate, population, or NOI realization member. \\
\Req{007} & The realization shall declare domain, real scientific codomains,
WCS/frame, indexing, measure, inner product, template scaling, phase, units,
support, boundaries, rank/null space, regularization, validity, and any
complex-transform conjugacy and Hermitian-adjoint convention. \\
\Req{008} & The authoritative estimator shall be exactly $N/D$ and $L_x$ as
defined in Section~\ref{sec:equations}. \\
\Req{009} & Every admitted $D(x)$ shall be finite, real to declared tolerance,
and strictly positive; an invalid $D$ is typed unavailability or failure, never
amplitude zero. \\
\Req{010} & Complete declared influence support shall be required. Partial
support, renormalization, extension, imputation, background subtraction,
learned taper, and signal-derived support are excluded. \\
\Req{011} & The full fixed-state response $R_t(x,y)$ and its valid domain
shall remain exactly available or reconstructable; reduced kernels or beams
require established invariances and an explicit measure. \\
\Req{012} & ``Optimal'' shall mean minimum conditional variance among
fixed-state linear unbiased estimators only under exact authorized inverse-
covariance GLS premises; weaker weighting carries no optimality claim. \\
\Req{013} & Every realization shall identify one owner-selected \AO{001}
weighting alternative separately for its parent class. No option in this draft
is a default. \\
\Req{014} & A parent coefficient shall retain only its declared option-specific
role; name, sign, units, reciprocal, or diagonal form shall not imply
covariance, precision, inverse variance, or independence. \\
\Req{015} & Requested, effective, observation-resolved, realized, and published
state shall remain distinct. State shall be externally declared or learned
once from the exact parent and external inputs, frozen, generation-identified,
and applied without target-dependent update. \\
\Req{016} & Observation and coadd state generations shall remain separate and
shall not be substituted for one another. \\
\Req{017} & Every compatible NOI member shall receive the identical frozen
state, transformation, support, normalization, approximation, and failure
rules as the corresponding signal realization. \\
\Req{018} & NOI-informed update shall create an immutable successor generation;
per-member relearning shall be a different, unavailable-in-v0.1 method. \\
\Req{019} & The method shall have no automatic selector or fallback. A
requested unavailable route shall fail closed without silent substitution. \\
\Req{020} & When exact matching covariance authority exists, conditional
covariance shall be $C_{\rm cond}=LC_{\rm parent}L^{\mathsf T}$. \\
\Req{021} & $D^{-1}$ shall be called marginal conditional variance only under
the exact inverse-covariance GLS premises; otherwise $D$ is normalization. \\
\Req{022} & Uncertainty availability and all U1--U7 budget terms shall be
truthful and role-separated; missing covariance, cross-covariance, or entries
shall be unavailable rather than zero or independent. \\
\Req{023} & The public signal product shall be the role-complete atomic bundle
defined in Section~\ref{sec:product-roles}. \\
\Req{024} & Failure of any required signal-bundle member shall fail the entire
bundle; a partial bundle shall not be published as complete. \\
\Req{025} & Conditional covariance, frozen-NOI uncertainty, response, and
state/lineage companions shall be independently atomic and qualified by exact
estimand, population, unit, support, validity, lifecycle, and named-use policy. \\
\Req{026} & \Disabled{}, \Unavailable{}, \Failed{}, \Complete{}, and
\Superseded{} shall remain distinct immutable lifecycle states. \\
\Req{027} & No numerator, denominator, kernel, PSD, response slice, inverse
scale, standardized field, or intermediate shall be public without a complete
science-product role and policy. \\
\Req{028} & The product contract shall preserve a first-class FLT to FRUIT
handoff containing filtered quantity, template, response, valid support,
units/calibration, method/state identity, uncertainty availability, and
provenance without undocumented implementation state. \\
\Req{029} & No FLT artifact or profile shall define FRUIT source modeling,
subtraction/add-back, recurrence, learning, stopping, restart, selection,
response, uncertainty, or interpretation. \\
\Req{030} & Detection, candidate selection, peaks with scientific meaning,
fitting, deblending, catalogs, significance, completeness, purity, morphology,
and SRC ownership shall remain outside scope. \\
\Req{031} & Posterior/Wiener sky reconstruction, ordinary convolution,
data-thresholded destriping, adaptive edge/background methods, and the
historical high-pass/delta case shall remain separate methods.
\texttt{SCI-FLT-FIXED} shall remain a separate protected package. \\
\Req{032} & All six authored option families shall receive explicit scientific-
owner disposition before any affected numerical, publication, covariance,
handoff, persistence, or validation route is available. \\
\Req{033} & Any approximate realization shall pass one selected \AO{002}
envelope against the exact $N/D$ operator over its complete declared validity
domain; iteration count or tail cap alone is not evidence. \\
\Req{034} & Scientific authority, implementation conformity, validation,
achieved performance, readiness, and production shall be recorded as separate
claims with separate evidence and owners. \\
\Req{035} & FLT shall own producer facts, named-use policies, required actions,
and failure semantics; VAL may register and evaluate immutable profiles but
shall not invent them. \\
\Req{036} & Parent and template calibration dependence shall remain joint.
Point-source flux, matched-filter beam/solid angle, extended-source fidelity,
and calibration covariance require exact separate authority. \\
\Req{037} & A coadd application shall retain exact contributing-observation
membership and parent provenance without asserting filter/coadd commutation. \\
\Req{038} & Every product and companion shall bind the full realization tuple,
immutable provenance, and selected persistence/reconstruction contract needed
for audit and reanalysis. \\
\Req{039} & This Stage B draft and every unselected option shall make no
implementation, conformity, validation, achieved-performance, readiness,
production, scientific-freeze, or Unity claim. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\section{Falsifiable scientific predictions}
\label{sec:predictions}

Each prediction is conditional on its cited assumptions and is falsified by
one conforming counterexample within the declared validity domain. A failed
prediction falsifies the affected scientific or conformity claim; it does not
authorize a fallback.

\begin{longtable}{p{0.25\linewidth}p{0.55\linewidth}p{0.10\linewidth}}
\toprule
Prediction & Falsifiable statement & Primary assumptions \\
\midrule
\endhead
\Pred{001} & An exact unit-amplitude matching template at admitted $y$ gives
$R_t(y,y)=1$. & 003--006 \\
\Pred{002} & At fixed state, scaling a matching noiseless template by $A$
scales the estimate by exactly $A$. & 003--006 \\
\Pred{003} & For conditionally zero-mean noise and a matching template,
$\operatorname{E}[\widehat A(y)\mid\mathrm{state}_g]=A$. & 003--007 \\
\Pred{004} & A location missing any influence-support dependency is never
published as a numerical amplitude. & 004,006 \\
\Pred{005} & Nonfinite, nonreal-beyond-tolerance, zero, or negative $D$ never
produces amplitude zero as a substitute. & 005--006 \\
\Pred{006} & Observation-parent and coadd-parent applications with otherwise
similar inputs retain distinct parent and state identities. & 001,010 \\
\Pred{007} & Every compatible NOI member has the same fixed $L$, valid support,
normalization, and failure decisions as its signal realization. & 010--011 \\
\Pred{008} & Under exact matching covariance authority, empirical covariance
of repeated fixed-state realizations converges to
$LC_{\rm parent}L^{\mathsf T}$ within declared sampling uncertainty. & 008--011 \\
\Pred{009} & Without exact inverse-covariance GLS premises, removing any
$D^{-1}$ variance label changes no amplitude value but removes the unsupported
uncertainty claim. & 005,008--009 \\
\Pred{010} & Any approximation accepted under \AO{002} satisfies every
normalization, unit-response, response, support/null, and covariance bound on
the full test domain. & 012--013 \\
\Pred{011} & Changing a scientifically consequential realization field changes
the realization or method identity and never mutates an existing complete
product. & 010, 013, 015 \\
\Pred{012} & Failure of one required signal-bundle member prevents a
\Complete{} signal bundle. & 015 \\
\Pred{013} & Failure of an optional covariance or NOI companion leaves a
complete signal bundle complete unless its exact named-use policy requires
that companion. & 009, 013, 015 \\
\Pred{014} & The output unit is always $[m]/[t]$; a rescaling $t\mapsto c t$
maps $\widehat A\mapsto\widehat A/c$ and preserves the modeled signal
$\widehat A t$. & 003,014 \\
\Pred{015} & A response reduced to one kernel fails its validity predicate when
tested where the required invariances do not hold. & 002,013 \\
\Pred{016} & Requesting an unavailable weighting, covariance, state,
approximation, handoff, or profile route never silently selects another one. & 015 \\
\Pred{017} & A filtered signal bundle plus its selected \AO{005} lineage can
answer every documented FLT-side handoff query without undocumented
implementation state. & 013,015 \\
\Pred{018} & No conforming output alone can be interpreted as a detection,
catalog entry, posterior sky reconstruction, FRUIT result, achieved-performance
claim, readiness decision, or production decision. & 001--015 \\

\section{Unselected authored option sets}
\label{sec:authored-options}

All alternatives in this section are scientifically bounded candidates.
They share the exact identities, assumptions, consequences, observables or
bounds, failure rules, and validation consequences in both contract views
because this section is imported verbatim by both. None is selected. Every
parameter written as ``owner-set'' remains a required later disposition.

\subsection{\AO{001}: Weighting and noise authority}
\label{sec:ao001}

Observation and coadd parents require separate dispositions and state
generations even if the same alternative identity is selected.

Every alternative shall explicitly bind the map chart, WCS metric, sampling,
units, fixed windows, complete influence support, and boundary/edge rule. It
shall also state whether Fourier transformation, averaging, and radialization
are used. A used operation requires its phase, normalization, measure,
conjugacy or multiplicity, population, and aggregation conventions as
applicable; an unused operation is recorded as absent and supplies no implied
default. These declarations are part of the option identity even when the
operation is not applicable to its mathematical form.

Every alternative shall also bind its estimator or external-declaration
identity and version, declaring or learn-once algorithm, immutable inputs and
provenance, population and conditioning state, sufficient statistics or
theoretical authority, state generation, and estimator tolerances. For
\AOpt{001}{A} and \AOpt{001}{B}, this includes the parent-covariance
estimator/model from which $Q_x$ is authorized or derived; for
\AOpt{001}{C}, it includes the spectral estimator and averaging population;
for \AOpt{001}{D}, it includes the weaker-weight estimator or exact external
declaration. A generic label such as ``authorized covariance'' or ``learned
once'' does not satisfy this closure.

\subsubsection{\AOpt{001}{A}: exact inverse-covariance GLS}

\begin{description}
\item[Object and assumptions.] $Q_x$ is the authorized inverse, or constrained
Moore--Penrose inverse, of exact $C_{\rm parent}$ on the complete admitted
support and estimable subspace. Population, conditioning, chart, sampling,
units, constraints, rank, null space, and any regularization are identical for
$C_{\rm parent}$ and $Q_x$. Regularization is admissible only as part of the
authorized covariance model or an exact declared constraint, not as a hidden
numerical convenience. The parent-covariance estimator/model provenance and
the inverse-construction identity are bound as required by the family rule.
\item[Parent coefficient.] A coefficient may enter only if covariance authority
defines its exact place in $C_{\rm parent}$ or the inner-product measure. It is
not independently reinterpreted as precision.
\item[Consequences.] This is the sole alternative that can carry the GLS
minimum-conditional-variance claim and $D^{-1}$ marginal conditional variance,
subject to every premise. Response is the full $L_xt_y$; uncertainty is
$LC_{\rm parent}L^{\mathsf T}$. Matching-template amplitude unbiasedness still
requires zero conditional mean and complete support.
\item[Observables and bounds.] On the estimable parent subspace
$P_{\rm in}$, require
$\|P_{\rm in}(Q_xC_{\rm parent}-I)P_{\rm in}^{\mathsf T}\|
\leq\tau_{\rm inv}$,
identical declared null spaces, $e_D\leq\tau_{\rm id}$, and unit response
within $\tau_{\rm id}$, where the norm and owner-set numerical-identity
tolerances are bound to the realization. A nonzero scientific approximation
instead routes to \AOpt{001}{B} and \AO{002}.
\item[NOI, products, and failure.] Compatible NOI members use the same frozen
$Q_x$. Exact covariance authority and the selected \AO{003} representation
are qualified companions, not inferred signal fields. Missing authority,
population mismatch, rank/null disagreement, exceeded closure tolerance, or
invalid $D$ makes the covariance/optimality route \Unavailable{} or the
attempt \Failed{}; no fallback occurs.
\item[Validation consequence.] Validate inverse closure, null-space identity,
matching-template response, exact/approximation identity, fixed-NOI parity,
and covariance propagation over the full domain. A pointwise diagonal check is
insufficient.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{001}{B}: structured covariance-derived weighting}

\begin{description}
\item[Object and assumptions.] An authorized covariance family
$C(\theta,g)$ with declared population and state generation is represented by
a structured $Q_x(\theta,g)$ that approximates its inverse. Structure may be
block, sparse, separable, locally stationary, low-rank-plus-residual, or other
declared form; the exact structure, chart, units, window, boundaries, rank,
null space, and regularization are part of the option realization. Observation
and coadd models are independently learned or declared. Their covariance-
estimator/model provenance and structured-inverse construction are immutable
option fields.
\item[Parent coefficient.] A coefficient may be an explicitly modeled factor,
mask, or measure in $C(\theta,g)$, but it gains no covariance meaning beyond
that authorized model.
\item[Consequences.] $N/D$ preserves fixed-state matching-template unit
response when valid. ``Optimal'' and $D^{-1}$ variance are unavailable unless
the structure is proven exact, in which case \AOpt{001}{A} is the proper
identity. Conditional covariance, if authorized, is still
$LC_{\rm parent}L^{\mathsf T}$ and not the inverse of a displayed weight.
\item[Observables and bounds.] Declare the complete model-fit population and
residual statistic; bound inverse-action residual
$\|P_{\rm in}(Q_xC_{\rm parent}-I)P_{\rm in}^{\mathsf T}\|
\leq\epsilon_Q$ and every \AO{002} metric on the
declared domain. $\epsilon_Q$, norm, sampling, aggregation, unresolved modes,
and regularization path are owner-set realization fields.
\item[NOI, products, and failure.] The frozen structured state and its
generation apply identically to compatible NOI members. A structure summary
may be a qualified state companion under \AO{004}; it is not a public PSD or
covariance unless assigned that role. Model-population mismatch, uncovered
modes, exceeded residuals, nonpositive normalization, or reconstruction
failure is typed unavailability/failure with no substitution.
\item[Validation consequence.] Validate structure-specific reconstruction,
inverse-action residuals, response across nonstationary and edge domains,
support/null equality, \AO{002} bounds, uncertainty labels, and NOI parity.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{001}{C}: radially symmetrized average map-noise PSD weighting}

\begin{description}
\item[Object and population.] This is the explicitly examined historical
candidate, not a default. Choose a declared noise-estimation population
$\{n_j\}_{j=1}^{J}$: either externally authorized noise fields, or a declared
learn-once field derived from the exact parent. The latter is weaker spectral
weighting unless separate authority proves a noise-covariance interpretation.
No target, source, candidate, or NOI member may update it.
\item[Fourier, WCS, units, and estimator.] Declare one map chart with physical
coordinate $r_z$, WCS metric, sampling measure $\mu(z)$, transform phase
$\exp(-2\pi i k\!\cdot\!r_z)$, frequency units, normalization $\alpha$, and a
fixed predeclared window $W(z)$. For complete supported fields define
\[
 F_j(k)=\alpha\sum_z W(z)n_j(z)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot r_z}\mu(z),\qquad
 \overline P_b=
 \frac{\sum_{j,k\in B_b}w_{jk}|F_j(k)|^2}
      {\sum_{j,k\in B_b}w_{jk}}.
\]
Radial bin $B_b$ is defined by an owner-declared metric radius $\rho(k)$,
closed bin edges, mode multiplicity, conjugate-mode convention, member weights
$w_{jk}$, and averaging order. The units of $\overline P_b$ follow exactly
from $[n]^2$, $\mu$, $\alpha$, and the frequency measure and shall be recorded.
No background subtraction, extension, padding, adaptive taper, or
signal-derived window is introduced. The spectral-estimator identity/version,
immutable field provenance, sufficient statistics, and state-generation
lineage are bound to this definition.
\item[Realized weight, support, and regularization.] On admitted modes,
$q(k)=(\overline P_{b(k)}+\lambda_b)^{-1}$ times any separately declared
dimensionless mode mask, and $Q_x$ is the declared transform-domain action
restricted to complete influence support. Every $\lambda_b$, excluded mode,
window dependency, boundary model, rank, and null space is fixed in $g$.
Zero/negative/nonfinite bin estimates and bins without declared effective
sample size are unavailable, not infinite precision.
\item[Parent coefficient.] A parent coefficient may contribute only through a
predeclared member weight $w_{jk}$, sample measure, or fixed map-domain factor
whose statistical meaning and units are stated. It does not become covariance
or precision merely because $q$ is reciprocal.
\item[Consequences.] Radialization deliberately discards angular spectral
structure. It does not prove stationarity, isotropy, covariance authority, or
GLS optimality. $N/D$ remains matching-template normalized; $D$ is not
variance. Response includes the window, radial binning, null modes, boundaries,
and position dependence. $C_{\rm cond}$ needs independent parent-covariance
authority.
\item[Quantitative observables.] Record per-bin effective sample size,
dispersion before radialization, angular anisotropy statistic, member-to-member
dispersion, window leakage matrix or bound, null-mode set, and regularization
fraction $\lambda_b/\overline P_b$. Owner disposition shall set admissible
bounds and the complete test population; all \AO{002} metrics also apply.
\item[NOI, products, and failure.] Compatible NOI members receive the same
frozen $\overline P_b$, window, modes, support, and normalization. A PSD may be
a qualified state artifact only with exact meaning, units, population,
lifecycle, and policy. Missing population authority or conventions, invalid
bins, failed anisotropy/leakage bounds, incomplete support, or exceeded
\AO{002} bounds makes this route unavailable/failed without fallback.
\item[Validation consequence.] Recompute the declared sufficient statistics
from the bound population, test transform normalization and units, radial-bin
membership, phase and conjugacy, anisotropy and leakage bounds, support erosion,
unit response, full response, uncertainty nonclaims, and fixed-NOI parity.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{001}{D}: declared weaker positive-semidefinite weighting}

\begin{description}
\item[Object and assumptions.] $Q_x$ is an externally declared or learn-once,
frozen, positive-semidefinite linear weighting with explicit scientific
purpose but no covariance ancestry claim. Its coordinate action, units,
support, boundaries, window, rank, null space, regularization, state population,
and generation are complete. This alternative includes nonradial spectral or
map-domain reliability weighting that is not authorized as covariance-derived.
Its external declaration or learn-once estimator, version, immutable inputs,
provenance, sufficient statistics, and tolerances are bound to the generation.
\item[Parent coefficient.] A coefficient is only a declared reliability factor,
mask, or part of the inner-product measure. It is not variance or precision.
\item[Consequences.] Exact $N/D$ gives fixed-state matching-template unit
response on valid support. Minimum variance, $D^{-1}$ uncertainty, and
covariance interpretation are unavailable. Response may be nonlocal and
position-dependent; uncertainty requires independent authority.
\item[Observables and bounds.] Require Hermitian symmetry to
$\tau_{\rm herm}$, nonnegative quadratic form to $-\tau_{\rm psd}$, declared
rank/null closure, and all selected \AO{002} metrics. Tolerances, probe domain,
and aggregation are owner-set fields.
\item[NOI, products, and failure.] The identical frozen operator applies to
compatible NOI members. The weight may be a qualified state companion under
\AO{004}, not a noise product by implication. Failed positivity, undocumented
coefficients, state drift, incomplete support, invalid $D$, or uncertainty
mislabeling causes typed unavailability/failure and no fallback.
\item[Validation consequence.] Validate linearity, Hermitian/positive-
semidefinite bounds, rank/null identity, full response, support, normalization,
uncertainty labels, and NOI parity across both parent classes separately.
\end{description}

\subsection{\AO{002}: Quantitative approximation envelope}
\label{sec:ao002}

All alternatives compare one approximate realization with the exact $N/D$
operator using Section~\ref{sec:approx-metrics}. The test set shall cover every
declared parent class, state stratum, valid-support geometry, boundary class,
template phase/anchor class, rank/null regime, and response query used by a
named consumer. A finite sample is acceptable only with a declared covering
argument and regularity bound that extends the measured maximum to the full
domain.

\subsubsection{\AOpt{002}{A}: exact-identity envelope}

\begin{description}
\item[Assumptions and bounds.] No scientific approximation is admitted.
Require $\widetilde L=L$, $\widetilde D=D$, $\widetilde R_t=R_t$,
$\widetilde\Valid=\Valid$, and identical null spaces. Finite representation
differences may not exceed a bound $\tau_{\rm id}$ derived from and no larger
than the selected numerical-identity tolerance for the archived realization;
they may not change any classification, response, or published digit claimed
as significant. If covariance is published, require
$\widetilde C_{\rm cond}=C_{\rm cond}$ to the same identity contract.
\item[Test domain and aggregation.] Exhaust the finite declared domain or use
a proof-producing equivalence over all omitted points and modes. Aggregation
is the maximum; unresolved modes are not allowed.
\item[Consequences.] The approximate label is only a realization detail; the
scientific operator is exact under the numerical identity contract.
\item[Failure and method boundary.] Any discrepancy above $\tau_{\rm id}$,
support/null disagreement, or unproved mode fails this option. A change to
estimand, support, null space, state-learning rule, or failure semantics is a
new method; any other numerical-identity change is at least a new realization
and generation.
\item[Validation consequence.] Archive exact-versus-realized fieldwise maxima,
coverage proof, response closure, covariance closure when applicable, and
classification equality.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{002}{B}: strict uniform scientific envelope}

\begin{description}
\item[Assumptions and quantitative bounds.] On every point and declared mode
of $\mathcal T$, require
\[
 \sup e_D\leq10^{-3},\quad
 \sup e_A\leq10^{-3},\quad
 \frac{\|P_{\rm out}(\widetilde L-L)P_{\rm in}^{\mathsf T}\|_2}
      {\|P_{\rm out}LP_{\rm in}^{\mathsf T}\|_2}\leq10^{-3},\quad
 e_C\leq2\times10^{-3}
\]
when covariance is an authorized product. Require
$\Delta_{\rm supp}=\Delta_{\rm null}=0$. The response residual shall also obey
$\|P_{\rm out}(\widetilde R_t-R_t)P_{\rm anc}^{\mathsf T}\|_2/
\|P_{\rm out}R_tP_{\rm anc}^{\mathsf T}\|_2\leq10^{-3}$. Zero denominators
use a dimensionally matched owner-set absolute scale for the affected
operator, covariance, or response, tied to the declared input, output, and
template-amplitude conventions, never a silently chosen floor.
\item[Test domain and aggregation.] $P_{\rm in}$, $P_{\rm out}$,
$P_{\rm anc}$, their codomains, domain sampling, absolute scales,
state strata, and a covering proof are fixed before evaluation. All quoted
bounds are hard maxima or spectral norms; no percentile may hide an outlier.
There are no unresolved output-affecting modes.
\item[Consequences.] The realization is a bounded approximation to the same
estimand. The bound is an operator-conformance statement, not evidence of
astrophysical adequacy, optimality, or achieved sensitivity. The U4 budget
records the full bound; covariance consumers also inherit the $e_C$ bound.
\item[Failure and method boundary.] One exceeded bound, changed support/null
set, missing exact comparator, uncovered state stratum, or failed covering
proof fails the realization. Changing a numerical technique within these
bounds creates a new realization. Changing the envelope, estimand, support,
null space, data-dependent selection, state learning, or failure policy creates
a new method version requiring owner disposition.
\item[Validation consequence.] Evaluate all metrics with immutable exact and
approximate identities, report worst-case location/mode and signed residual,
repeat for both parent classes separately, and test matching-template injection
and authorized covariance propagation.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{002}{C}: named-use stratified envelope}

\begin{description}
\item[Assumptions and quantitative bounds.] A named use declares a primary
response region $\mathcal T_{\rm core}$ containing at least $99\%$ of the
declared exact response energy under its explicit measure, plus the remaining
valid region $\mathcal T_{\rm tail}$. Require everywhere
$e_D,e_A\leq10^{-2}$ and exact support/null equality. Require response-energy
RMS residual at most $10^{-2}$ on the core and integrated absolute response
residual at most $2\times10^{-2}$ of total exact response magnitude on the
tail. If covariance is authorized, require $e_C\leq5\times10^{-2}$ on each
declared consumer projection. These are ceilings; the owner may select tighter
profile-specific bounds but not looser ones under this identity.
\item[Test domain and aggregation.] Core/tail measure, energy definition,
consumer projections, sample covering, absolute zero-response scale, and state
strata are immutable profile fields. Every valid location is classified; an
unresolved mode makes the dependent named use unavailable.
\item[Consequences.] This option permits larger, explicitly budgeted response
and covariance discrepancy for a named use while preserving amplitude,
support, and null semantics. It cannot support an unprofiled consumer and
does not establish global optimality or performance.
\item[Failure and method boundary.] Exceeding any ceiling, changing the
core/tail partition after seeing results, concealing an unresolved mode, or
using the result outside its named profile fails the route. New partition,
ceilings, consumer projection, estimand, support/null, or failure semantics
create a new method/profile version; a numerically changed realization under
the same frozen profile is a new realization.
\item[Validation consequence.] Report hard pointwise maxima, core energy RMS,
tail integrated residual, covariance projection residuals, coverage proof,
and every unavailable mode. Validate each named use independently; aggregate
pass cannot erase a failed subprofile.
\end{description}

\subsection{\AO{003}: Conditional covariance representation}
\label{sec:ao003}

Every available alternative starts from independently authorized
$C_{\rm parent}$ for the same population, support, response, state, and units
as $L$. It represents $C_{\rm cond}=LC_{\rm parent}L^{\mathsf T}$; it does not
infer covariance from $D$, $Q$, or an NOI companion. Calibration terms and
cross-terms are included only with exact authority.

For each available alternative, the conditional-covariance estimator is the
declared fixed-state propagation $LC_{\rm parent}L^{\mathsf T}$, with only the
selected \AO{002} discrepancy where that alternative expressly permits it.
The companion shall bind the independently authorized parent-covariance
estimator or model identity and version, declaring or learning algorithm,
immutable inputs and provenance, population and conditioning, sufficient
statistics or theoretical authority, state generation, and every estimator
tolerance. \AOpt{003}{E} shall instead identify which of those estimator,
model, provenance, population, or conditioning authorities is missing. No
representation option supplies a covariance estimator by implication.

\subsubsection{\AOpt{003}{A}: exact explicit covariance}

\begin{description}
\item[Representation.] Materialize every authorized covariance entry on the
complete valid output domain with exact indexing, symmetry, units, population,
conditioning state, rank, null space, response and generation. No correlation
is omitted; authorized calibration blocks are explicit.
\item[Approximation and consumers.] None beyond the selected numerical identity
tolerance. All consumers whose domain and conditioning match may use the
matrix subject to named policy. Storage is quadratic in admitted samples.
\item[Lifecycle and failure.] The covariance is an independently atomic
qualified companion. Any missing entry, broken symmetry/positive-semidefinite
bound, rank/null mismatch, unit or population mismatch, or incomplete atomic
member makes it \Failed{} or \Unavailable{}; it never fills unknown entries
with zero.
\item[Validation consequence.] Recompute selected entries and quadratic forms
from $L$ and $C_{\rm parent}$, exhaust index/symmetry closure, verify units,
rank/null space, calibration blocks, and match empirical fixed-state ensembles
within declared sampling uncertainty.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{003}{B}: exact structured covariance}

\begin{description}
\item[Representation.] Persist an exact factorization or structured operator
whose queries reproduce every authorized entry and quadratic form of
$LC_{\rm parent}L^{\mathsf T}$ on the full valid domain. Structure, factors,
index maps, support, response, rank/null, regularization identity, population,
units, calibration blocks, and state generation are immutable.
\item[Approximation and consumers.] Scientific approximation is zero; a
reconstruction tolerance $\tau_C$ is an owner-set numerical-identity field.
All declared entry, marginal, block, draw, and quadratic-form queries are
supported; any unimplemented query is explicitly unavailable rather than
approximated. Storage is structure-dependent and less than full materialization
only when the exact structure permits it.
\item[Lifecycle and failure.] The structured state is an atomic companion.
Failed reconstruction, query-dependent drift, unbound environment facts,
rank/null mismatch, omitted calibration term, or residual above $\tau_C$
fails the companion and dependent consumers.
\item[Validation consequence.] Use adversarial and basis-spanning queries to
compare with direct $LC_{\rm parent}L^{\mathsf T}$, verify deterministic
reconstruction and all metadata, and test every advertised consumer query.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{003}{C}: authorized projected covariance}

\begin{description}
\item[Representation.] For one named consumer projection $P_c$, publish the
complete exact or \AO{002}-bounded covariance
$P_cLC_{\rm parent}L^{\mathsf T}P_c^{\mathsf T}$. The projection basis,
measure, domain, support, response, retained rank/null space, state, units,
population, calibration treatment, and reconstruction bound are immutable.
All correlations outside the projection are explicitly unknown.
\item[Approximation and consumers.] The owner selects exact projection or an
owner-set residual ceiling $\epsilon_{C,c}$ not exceeding the selected
\AO{002} covariance limit. Only the named projected consumer is admissible.
No diagonal, map-wide, independence, draw, or inverse-covariance use follows.
\item[Lifecycle and failure.] Each projection is an independently atomic
companion. Missing basis vectors, changed projection, rank loss, unbounded
omitted modes, calibration mismatch, or exceeded residual makes that consumer
route unavailable/failed without changing the signal bundle.
\item[Validation consequence.] Validate projection orthogonality/measure,
rank/null identity, exact projected entries and quadratic forms, residual
bounds, omitted-mode labels, and rejection of every unlisted consumer.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{003}{D}: exact lineage-resolvable covariance on demand}

\begin{description}
\item[Representation.] Persist no covariance values, but retain exact immutable
lineage sufficient to reconstruct $L$, $C_{\rm parent}$, domain/support,
response, units, population, state, rank/null space, regularization,
calibration terms, and the selected computation identity. Reconstruction must
not require undocumented implementation state.
\item[Approximation and consumers.] Each supported query is reconstructed
exactly within owner-set $\tau_C$ and yields an immutable qualified result with
its own lifecycle. Supported query classes and resource limits are declared;
unsupported queries are unavailable. This is not permission to substitute a
different covariance model later.
\item[Lifecycle and failure.] The lineage closure is the atomic companion until
a query result is produced. Missing inputs, nonreproducible environment facts,
version drift, failed reconstruction test, or residual above $\tau_C$ makes
the covariance route unavailable/failed.
\item[Validation consequence.] Before publication, perform and archive a
representative basis-spanning reconstruction, hash/identity closure, repeated
environment-independent result, and comparisons with direct propagation for
all advertised query classes.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{003}{E}: covariance unavailable}

\begin{description}
\item[Representation and assumptions.] No authorized matching
$C_{\rm parent}$ or defensible representation exists. Record the exact missing
authority or premise. No numerical covariance, marginal variance,
standardization, significance, or independence statement is published.
\item[Consequences and consumers.] The filtered amplitude signal may remain
\Complete{} if all signal requirements pass. Every consumer requiring
$C_{\rm cond}$ is \Unavailable{}. A separately qualified frozen-NOI companion
does not replace it.
\item[Lifecycle and failure.] This is typed unavailability, not a failed
attempt and not an all-zero matrix. Later authority creates a successor
companion or generation without mutating the predecessor.
\item[Validation consequence.] Validate absence of covariance-valued fields,
$D^{-1}$ variance labels, zero-filled matrices, significance products, and
consumers that silently assume independence.
\end{description}

\subsection{\AO{004}: Immutable state persistence}
\label{sec:ao004}

Every alternative binds the state-generation identifier, learning/declaring
algorithm and version, exact parent and external inputs, learning population,
template, $Q_x$, windows, rank/null, regularization, support, numerical identity,
environment-dependent facts, failure policy, and compatible-NOI parity.
Updates create successors; predecessors are not rewritten.

\subsubsection{\AOpt{004}{A}: full state materialization}

\begin{description}
\item[Persistence.] Persist every realized state element used by $L$, response,
support, normalization, uncertainty, and named-use policy, together with exact
indexing, units, hashes, algorithm/version, inputs, population, and generation.
No reconstruction from learning data is needed. Storage scales with full state.
\item[Numerical identity and reconstruction test.] Reloaded state shall match
the archived materialization bit-for-bit or through a lossless canonical
serialization; application results shall match within owner-set
$\tau_{\rm state}$ no larger than the chosen \AO{002} identity bound.
\item[Audit, reanalysis, and NOI.] This gives the broadest audit and reanalysis
independence from the original environment. Every compatible NOI member binds
the same archived state hash. A successor has a new hash and generation.
\item[Failure.] Missing element, failed hash, ambiguous indexing/unit,
environment override, or reconstruction residual above $\tau_{\rm state}$
fails state admission and all dependent products; no relearning fallback.
\item[Validation consequence.] Round-trip every field, compare operator and
response on a basis-spanning domain, verify NOI state hashes, and demonstrate
predecessor immutability after successor creation.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{004}{B}: structured compact state}

\begin{description}
\item[Persistence.] Persist a declared compact factorization, parameterization,
or sufficient-state representation plus exact reconstruction semantics. Bind
all factors, index maps, conventions, tolerances, algorithm/version, original
inputs/population, environment facts, and generation. Storage is structure-
dependent; discarded information is forbidden unless proved irrelevant to
every supported query and operator action.
\item[Numerical identity and reconstruction test.] Reconstruct full operator
actions, response queries, support/null decisions, and normalizations within
owner-set $\tau_{\rm state}$ and the selected \AO{002} envelope on a complete
covering domain. Unsupported queries are explicitly unavailable.
\item[Audit, reanalysis, and NOI.] Audit/reanalysis is limited to the advertised
query set. Compatible NOI members bind the identical compact-state identity.
Changing structure, factors, tolerance, or query set creates a successor
generation and may create a new method under \AO{002}.
\item[Failure.] Undeclared discarded state, nonunique reconstruction,
unbound environment dependence, uncovered query, state drift, or exceeded
residual fails the route without full-state or relearning fallback.
\item[Validation consequence.] Use basis-spanning and adversarial queries,
support/null boundary cases, repeated reconstruction across declared
environments, hash closure, and NOI parity. Report unsupported queries.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{004}{C}: exact lineage reconstruction}

\begin{description}
\item[Persistence.] Persist the complete immutable parent and external-input
identities, learning population, template, algorithm/version, declared
environment, numerical libraries or mathematical identities as scientifically
consequential, random seeds when any, tolerances, failure policy, and lineage
needed to rerun \emph{DeclareOrLearnOnce}. No undocumented state is allowed.
\item[Numerical identity and reconstruction test.] Before any dependent product
is complete, reconstruct the state independently and require canonical state,
operator, response, support/null, and normalization agreement within owner-set
$\tau_{\rm state}$ and the selected \AO{002} envelope. Bitwise identity is
required for fields declared discrete or exact.
\item[Audit, reanalysis, and NOI.] Reanalysis depends on continuing availability
of every lineage input and authorized environment. NOI members reference the
reconstructed frozen state identity, never rerun learning per member. Any
NOI-informed update creates a successor lineage.
\item[Failure.] Missing/mutable input, unavailable algorithm version,
unreproducible environment, stochastic ambiguity, failed closure, or exceeded
tolerance makes state and dependent routes unavailable/failed; no inferred
substitute or relearning fallback exists.
\item[Validation consequence.] Perform two independent reconstructions, close
all identities/hashes, compare complete operator/response cover, test archival
availability and environment declarations, and demonstrate identical NOI use.
\end{description}

\subsection{\AO{005}: Response, product, and FLT to FRUIT interface}
\label{sec:ao005}

Every alternative retains the same role-complete signal bundle and preserves
the exact operator, filtered quantity, template, full response meaning, valid
support, units/calibration, method/state identity, uncertainty availability,
and provenance. The choice concerns response/state representation and query
availability, not the scientific response itself and not FRUIT behavior.

\subsubsection{\AOpt{005}{A}: full response materialization}

\begin{description}
\item[Representation and storage.] Materialize $R_t(x,y)$ for every admitted
output $x$ and every declared template anchor $y$, with exact index maps,
measure, units, valid support, state/operator identity, template generation,
and any authorized calibration relation. Storage is generally quadratic in
the two response domains; no invariance reduction is assumed.
\item[Exactness and queries.] Values match direct $L_xt_y$ within owner-set
$\tau_R$ no larger than the selected \AO{002} response bound. Entry, slice,
integral, moment, beam/solid-angle, or other queries are supported only when
their measure and validity policy are declared. A materialized matrix does not
itself authorize a reduced scientific interpretation.
\item[Consumers and handoff.] Any named consumer, including a future FRUIT
contract, may use only its registered query/profile. The signal bundle and
response companion supply all FLT-side identity without undocumented state.
\item[Lifecycle and failure.] Response is an independently atomic companion
or required handoff member according to named policy. Missing entries,
index/unit mismatch, invalid-support leakage, exceeded $\tau_R$, or incomplete
lineage fails response-dependent routes; it does not define FRUIT behavior or
retroactively change the signal unless required by that signal policy.
\item[Validation consequence.] Exhaust indexing and support, compare basis
slices with direct $L_xt_y$, test asymmetry/nonstationarity retention, units,
calibration references, query policies, and atomic lifecycle.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{005}{B}: exact structured response with documented query contract}

\begin{description}
\item[Representation and storage.] Persist a compact exact factorization or
mathematical response representation plus state needed to answer a finite
declared query vocabulary. Bind operator/template/state versions, index maps,
coordinate measures, support/null rules, units/calibration, approximation
identity, and provenance. Storage follows the structure; no stationarity,
isotropy, symmetry, or locality is presumed without proof.
\item[Exactness and queries.] Every advertised query reconstructs $L_xt_y$
within owner-set $\tau_R$ and the selected \AO{002} envelope. Query vocabulary
may include entries, local slices, named projections, or response-applied
vectors. Unadvertised queries and invalid locations are typed unavailable.
\item[Consumers and handoff.] Each consumer binds the exact query vocabulary
and validity domain. A future FRUIT contract can consume the interface without
implementation knowledge, but must separately define its science.
\item[Lifecycle and failure.] The structured response and query contract are
an atomic companion. Hidden environment state, unbound structure assumptions,
unsupported queries presented as zeros, failed reconstruction, or response
residual above $\tau_R$ fails dependent routes with no switch to a reduced
kernel.
\item[Validation consequence.] Use basis-spanning and adversarial response
queries across boundaries and state strata; disprove undeclared invariances,
verify exact unavailable responses for unsupported queries, and close all
lineage and units.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{005}{C}: exact lineage-resolvable response on demand}

\begin{description}
\item[Representation and storage.] Materialize no response array. Persist the
complete immutable lineage needed to reconstruct $L$, $t_y$, valid domains,
support/null decisions, coordinate measure, units/calibration, state,
approximation, and failure policy. This may share an \AO{004} lineage only
when that selected alternative exposes every required response fact.
\item[Exactness and queries.] Before product completion, independently
reconstruct a declared basis-spanning sample within owner-set $\tau_R$ and the
selected \AO{002} envelope. Supported on-demand query classes and resource
limits are fixed. A later query creates an immutable qualified response result;
unsupported or unreconstructable queries are unavailable.
\item[Consumers and handoff.] The FLT to FRUIT interface contains the lineage
identity and documented scientific reconstruction contract, never a pointer
to undocumented implementation state. A future FRUIT named use must require
only supported queries or commission a successor FLT product contract.
\item[Lifecycle and failure.] Missing lineage, unavailable template/state,
version/environment drift, failed basis test, exceeded $\tau_R$, or query
nondeterminism makes response-dependent handoff unavailable/failed. The
filtered amplitude map may remain complete under its own policy.
\item[Validation consequence.] Perform two independent response
reconstructions, compare direct $L_xt_y$ over the covering set, verify all
identities and archive availability, test query rejection, and demonstrate
that no undocumented state is needed.
\end{description}

\subsection{\AO{006}: VAL profile granularity}
\label{sec:ao006}

All alternatives preserve six scientifically distinct verdict roles:
parent admission (PA), state admission (SA), public signal publication (SP),
conditional covariance use (CU), optional NOI companion use (NU), and FLT to
FRUIT handoff (FH). FLT supplies immutable producer facts, named-use policy,
consumer action, and failure semantics. VAL only registers and evaluates the
versioned profiles. An aggregate never changes a role verdict.

\subsubsection{\AOpt{006}{A}: six role-separated profiles}

\begin{description}
\item[Profile set and facts.] Maintain one immutable versioned FLT-owned
profile for each of PA, SA, SP, CU, NU, and FH. Each contains only the producer
facts, option identities, validity predicates, lifecycle states, and evidence
references needed for that role.
\item[Policy and action.] Every profile names admissible consumers and exact
pass, unavailable, and failed actions. PA/SA failure prevents dependent SP;
CU, NU, and FH may be unavailable without invalidating SP unless SP's named
policy explicitly requires one. No role is inferred from another.
\item[Aggregation and concealment.] A release view may display six verdicts
but has no scalar pass. Combining roles would conceal scientifically distinct
failures and is forbidden under this option.
\item[Versioning and failure.] Any fact, threshold, selected AO, policy, or
action change versions only the affected profile plus declared dependents.
Missing facts yield typed unavailability; evaluator failure yields failed.
\item[Validation consequence.] Test all $5^6$ lifecycle combinations by rule
or exhaustive generated truth table, dependency propagation, consumer action,
version isolation, and proof that no CU/NU/FH failure silently changes SP.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{006}{B}: three layered profiles with mandatory subverdicts}

\begin{description}
\item[Profile set and facts.] Use an Admission profile containing separate PA
and SA subverdicts, a Publication profile containing SP plus separate CU and NU
subverdicts, and a Handoff profile containing FH. Every subverdict retains its
own producer facts, named-use policy, action, lifecycle, and selected options.
\item[Policy and action.] Layer-level action is a deterministic vector-valued
rule over subverdicts. Admission blocks SP only according to explicit PA/SA
dependencies. CU and NU actions affect only named consumers; FH is independent
of FRUIT science and cannot upgrade SP.
\item[Aggregation and concealment.] A displayed layer scalar may be a warning
summary but cannot replace, overwrite, or be consumed without the complete
subverdict vector. Combining CU or NU with SP would conceal optional-companion
failure if only the scalar were retained, so scalar-only persistence is
forbidden.
\item[Versioning and failure.] Profiles and subpolicies are independently
versioned; an aggregate version binds the exact component versions. Missing
subverdicts make the layer unavailable; evaluation faults fail only affected
subverdicts and declared dependents.
\item[Validation consequence.] Exhaust subverdict transition tables, verify
vector preservation through registry and consumer interfaces, test component
version changes, and demonstrate that every distinct role failure remains
visible and actionable.
\end{description}

\subsubsection{\AOpt{006}{C}: one composite profile with a six-role verdict vector}

\begin{description}
\item[Profile set and facts.] Use one immutable composite profile only if it
contains six separately addressable PA, SA, SP, CU, NU, and FH verdict records,
each with complete producer facts, named-use policy, action, lifecycle,
evidence, and selected-option identity.
\item[Policy and action.] Consumers request a named vector component, never a
global Boolean. The composite defines an explicit dependency graph and
vector-valued transition function. Unavailable and failed remain distinct per
role.
\item[Aggregation and concealment.] A scalar aggregate is scientifically
inadmissible because it necessarily conceals at least one distinct role
failure. A human summary may list counts only alongside the full vector and
cannot drive action.
\item[Versioning and failure.] The composite version binds six component
versions and dependency-graph version. Missing one component makes only that
role and declared dependents unavailable, while corruption of the composite
identity fails the entire profile record.
\item[Validation consequence.] Prove lossless round-trip of all six verdicts,
exhaust the dependency graph and action table, reject scalar-only consumers,
test independent failures and version changes, and confirm VAL adds no policy.
\end{description}

\subsection{Option-set closure and unavailable routes}

Until the scientific owner selects and fully parameterizes an alternative in
each family, the following routes remain unavailable: weighting realization
and any corresponding optimality label (\AO{001}); approximate-operator
conformity (\AO{002}); conditional-covariance publication or use
(\AO{003}); state audit/reconstruction and dependent completion
(\AO{004}); response-dependent named use and FLT to FRUIT handoff
(\AO{005}); and registered validation/publication policy (\AO{006}).
Selection of an option does not by itself establish implementation conformity,
validation, achieved performance, readiness, or production.
